output.brief:
The October night premium shortfall was caused by a change made on 22 Oct by an Ardentra consultant. It was logged as a "label correction" with no testing. In fact it applied a template that moved the NSP-02 night premium start from 20:00 to 22:00. The platform's audit trail, which can't be edited, shows this was the only pay-rule edit. Internal audit recalculated all 158 night workers. 147 were underpaid by exactly 0.33 × hourly rate × the hours worked between 20:00 and 22:00. The 11 paid correctly work 22:00–06:00. Re-running October with the start time set back to 20:00 matched expected pay for all 158. This was on release 7.4, so the release did not cause it. Ardentra's data-quality account doesn't hold up: flagged records were underpaid no more often than unflagged ones. Day workers with flagged records were paid correctly.

Recommended: have Ardentra restore the 20:00 start and prove it in test before 24 Nov. Then pay everyone short through an off-cycle payment. Do not suspend the HR team or accept the clause 14.3 cost. Do not roll back 7.4, because the November tax table needs it. Review Ardentra's change-classification and testing practice. Whether the rota trial or the pay errors drove the fall in overtime cover is still unclear. Pausing the trial now is premature. Fixing the pay is the first step. I'm highly confident in the cause.
